A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpodNet and its UBG, PNP and E2E variants. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic precision-matrix recovery experiments, including reconstruction, support recovery and sparsity/positive-definiteness analyses in Figures 4–6.

after.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 report original synthetic experiments and graph learning on Animals. Appendix B.3 adds empirical measurements of GLAD outputs' positive-definiteness.

M1.justification: The Schur-complement framework and three model families remain. However, v2 normalizes the final-layer preactivation instead of the network output, adds a quadratic-form input to g, and replaces its exponential output activation with absolute value. The stepsize network also changes from whole-matrix input to column input, with revised widths. These are actual procedural refinements, not merely expanded descriptions.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic Gaussian precision-matrix recovery only. v2 adds synthetic-to-real transfer for graph inference on Animals, comprising 33 species and 102 binary attributes (Section 5.2). This introduces a substantive new data domain and evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: v1 principally benchmarks recovery against Oracle GLasso and examines GLAD's structural failures separately. v2 adds inverse Ledoit-Wolf and OAS estimators, includes both GLAD outputs in reconstruction/support comparisons, and evaluates EGFM alongside GLasso on Animals (Figures 4–6). DeepGraph remains discussed rather than experimentally compared.

E3.justification: GLasso tuning changes from ground-truth oracle selection to sample-based cross-validation. v2 uses 1,000 training pairs for every learned model, versus 100 for v1's UBG, and expands the p=n=50 evaluation to several dimensions and sample-size sweeps. Initialization changes from (S+0.1I)^−1 to (S+I)^−1, and learning rates are revised. Animals introduces graph construction, Louvain partitioning and modularity evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds sample-size sensitivity (Figure 5), training-time conditioning and sparsity diagnostics (Figure 3), and GLAD positive-definiteness frequencies (Appendix B.3). v1's post-hoc GLAD threshold sweep and illustrative precision-matrix comparisons disappear. The original instability example without normalization is retained as v2 Figure 7, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions display shaded bands without explaining their statistical meaning. Neither reports training seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence levels or significance tests. The additional curves do not establish a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v1 Figure 4 reports minimum PNP test NMSE of 0.316 against Oracle GLasso's 0.405. v2 replaces this fixed-setting comparison with broader reconstruction and sample-size results, plus GLAD SPD frequencies. New Animals modularities are 0.78 for UBG, 0.61 for GLasso and 0.86 for EGFM (Figure 6). Changed protocols prevent interpreting the revised scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix A.2's Proposition A.1 and proof characterizing the regularization threshold yielding a diagonal GLasso solution. The core SPD-preservation and efficient inverse-update propositions, their proofs, and the spectral-perturbation argument remain. Recasting the update using u and v is principally an equivalent mathematical presentation.

C1.justification: The central claim of a first architecture guaranteeing jointly sparse and SPD outputs remains. v2 drops the abstract/conclusion's explicit comparative claim of a larger function class or higher expressivity than existing approaches, focusing the contribution on structural guarantees and demonstrated effectiveness instead.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends the applicability discussion: it interprets the sample-size results as evidence of suitability for sample-deficient recovery and Animals as evidence of synthetic-to-real generalization. It qualifies EGFM's modularity advantage through its clustering-specific inductive bias. v1's explanation that UBG's stronger inductive bias permits fewer training examples is removed; the existing spectral-instability explanation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies g's hidden layers, batch size, threshold scaling for PNP/E2E, and GLAD's implementation source/defaults, alongside revised architecture and training details. v2 also states that PyTorch implementations accompany the submission and will become public. Much existing information is relocated, while v1's RTX 2080 SUPER and EPYC 7302 hardware disclosure is omitted.

R1.justification: The same three research strands remain, but v2 sharpens positioning around simultaneous structural constraints and adds references including Shlezinger et al., Adler and Öktem, Arridge et al., and EGFM. Several optimal-transport, nonsmooth-Riemannian and application references are removed. GLAD's citation-year correction refers to the same work and is not a new comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related work and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. The Graphical Lasso and competing-method discussions are consolidated, experiments are organized into synthetic and real-data subsections, and appendices are reorganized into experimental details and model analyses. A reproducibility statement is added.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially rebuilt with multi-panel benchmarks, sample-size plots, Animals graph visualizations and new diagnostic figures. v1's threshold plots and matrix heatmaps are removed. Figure 1 is relocated, the instability figure moves to the appendix, and conference formatting changes headers, author layout and typography.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the narrow empirical validation in v1: matched training sizes, broader recovery baselines, sample-size sensitivity and Animals transfer let readers assess practical advantages and applicability beyond one synthetic setting. Additional implementation details support reproduction. Important caveats remain: uncertainty bands are undefined, and replacing exponential g with absolute value introduces an unresolved zero case in the strict-positivity guarantee. Nevertheless, the retained core theorem and substantially more informative evaluation support a major overall improvement.
